module Bench where

import Prelude
import Effect (Effect)
import Effect.Console (log)

foreign import benchNow :: Effect Number
foreign import opaque :: forall a. a -> Effect a
foreign import formatNumber :: Number -> String

-- Returns microseconds per invocation. The native driver consumes every numeric result
-- and checks the final result against the separately validated warm-up value.
foreign import measureBatch :: Int -> Int -> Effect Int -> Effect Number

calibrate :: Int -> Effect Int -> Int -> Number -> Effect Int
calibrate expected act iterations target = do
  elapsed <- measureBatch iterations expected act
  if elapsed >= target || iterations >= 16777216
    then pure iterations
    else calibrate expected act (iterations * 2) (target / 2.0)

runBench :: Effect Unit -> Effect Int -> Effect Number
runBench describe act = do
  log "--------------------------------------------------\n\n(Test)\n"
  describe
  log "\n(Output & Warm-up)\n"
  out <- act
  log (show out)
  void act
  void act
  iterations <- calibrate out act 1 10000.0
  d1 <- measureBatch iterations out act
  d2 <- measureBatch iterations out act
  d3 <- measureBatch iterations out act
  d4 <- measureBatch iterations out act
  d5 <- measureBatch iterations out act
  d6 <- measureBatch iterations out act
  d7 <- measureBatch iterations out act
  d8 <- measureBatch iterations out act
  d9 <- measureBatch iterations out act
  d10 <- measureBatch iterations out act
  let best = min (min (min (min d1 d2) (min d3 d4)) (min (min d5 d6) (min d7 d8))) (min d9 d10)
  log ("\n(Execution time - best of 10)\n\n" <> formatNumber best <> " μs\n")
  log ("Batch iterations: " <> show iterations)
  pure best

runBenchSync :: Effect Unit -> Effect String -> Effect Number
runBenchSync describe act = do
  log "--------------------------------------------------\n\n(Test)\n"

data List a = Nil | Cons a (List a)

range start end = go end Nil
  where
  go curr acc =
    if curr < start then acc
    else go (curr - 1) (Cons curr acc)

filterEvens :: List Int -> List Int
filterEvens lst = go lst Nil
  where
  go Nil acc = acc
  go (Cons x xs) acc =
    if x `mod` 2 == 0 then go xs (Cons x acc)
    else go xs acc

foldl :: ∀ a b. (b -> a -> b) -> b -> List a -> b
foldl _ acc Nil = acc
foldl f acc (Cons x xs) = foldl f (f acc x) xs

sumEvens :: Int -> Int
sumEvens n = foldl (+) 0 (filterEvens (range 1 n))

describe :: Effect Unit
describe = log "List Processing (900 elements):"

act :: Effect Int
act = do
  dummy <- Bench.opaque 900
  pure ( sumEvens dummy)

module Test.Church where

import Prelude
import Effect (Effect)
import Effect.Console (log)
import Bench as Bench

-- Church Numerals represents integers entirely as functions.
-- This heavily benchmarks currying, closure allocation,
-- and higher-order function applications.
type Church a = (a -> a) -> a -> a

zeroC :: forall a. Church a
zeroC _ x = x

succC :: forall a. Church a -> Church a
succC n f x = f (n f x)

addC :: forall a. Church a -> Church a -> Church a
addC m n f x = m f (n f x)

mulC :: forall a. Church a -> Church a -> Church a
mulC m n f x = m (n f) x

fromInt :: Int -> Church Int
fromInt 0 = zeroC
fromInt n = succC (fromInt (n - 1))

toInt :: Church Int -> Int
toInt n = n (\x -> x + 1) 0

c10 :: Int -> Church Int
c10 n = fromInt n

c100 :: Int -> Church Int
c100 n = mulC (c10 n) (c10 n)

c10k :: Int -> Church Int
c10k n = mulC (c100 n) (c100 n)

c100k :: Int -> Church Int
c100k n = mulC (c10k n) (c10 n)

describe :: Effect Unit
describe = log "Church Numerals (100k Closure Applications):"

act :: Effect Int
act = do
  dummy <- Bench.opaque 10
  pure ( toInt (c100k dummy))

module Test.Primes where

import Prelude
import Effect (Effect)
import Effect.Console (log)
import Bench as Bench

-- Implementation of the Sieve of Eratosthenes using strict Lists.
-- This benchmark heavily tests:
-- 1. Non-tail recursion (sieve depth is equal to the number of primes found).
-- 2. Massive Garbage Collection: 'filter' creates entirely new lists thousands of times.
-- 3. Closure invocation: The lambda passed to 'filter' captures the prime 'p'.

data List a = Nil | Cons a (List a)

range :: Int -> Int -> List Int
range start end = go end Nil
  where
  go curr acc =
    if curr < start
    then acc
    else go (curr - 1) (Cons curr acc)

filter :: forall a. (a -> Boolean) -> List a -> List a
filter p lst = go lst Nil
  where
  go Nil acc = reverse acc
  go (Cons x xs) acc =
    if p x
    then go xs (Cons x acc)
    else go xs acc

reverse :: forall a. List a -> List a
reverse lst = go lst Nil
  where
  go Nil acc = acc
  go (Cons x xs) acc = go xs (Cons x acc)

-- Strict, non-tail-recursive Sieve
sieve :: List Int -> List Int
sieve Nil = Nil
sieve (Cons p xs) = Cons p (sieve (filter (\x -> not (x `mod` p == 0)) xs))

sumList :: List Int -> Int
sumList lst = go lst 0
  where
  go Nil acc = acc
  go (Cons x xs) acc = go xs (acc + x)

-- Sum of all primes up to 20,000
-- There are 2262 primes, so sieve recurses 2262 times (safe for JS stack).
-- The total iterations across all filters will be around ~22 million.
describe :: Effect Unit
describe = log "Prime Sieve (sum primes up to 500):"

act :: Effect Int
act = do
  dummy <- Bench.opaque 500
  pure ( sumList (sieve (range 2 dummy)))

module Test.RBTree where

import Prelude hiding (max)

import Effect (Effect)
import Effect.Console (log)
import Bench as Bench

-- The ultimate functional benchmark: Chris Okasaki's Red-Black Tree.
-- This heavily tests complex pattern matching, structural sharing,
-- rapid allocation/deallocation of ADTs, and balancing rotations.

data Color = R | B
data Tree = E | T Color Tree Int Tree

balance :: Color -> Tree -> Int -> Tree -> Tree
balance B (T R (T R a x b) y c) z d = T R (T B a x b) y (T B c z d)
balance B (T R a x (T R b y c)) z d = T R (T B a x b) y (T B c z d)
balance B a x (T R (T R b y c) z d) = T R (T B a x b) y (T B c z d)
balance B a x (T R b y (T R c z d)) = T R (T B a x b) y (T B c z d)
balance color a x b = T color a x b

insert :: Int -> Tree -> Tree
insert x s = makeBlack (ins x s)

ins :: Int -> Tree -> Tree
ins x E = T R E x E
ins x (T color a y b) =
  if x < y then balance color (ins x a) y b
  else if x > y then balance color a y (ins x b)
  else T color a y b

makeBlack :: Tree -> Tree
makeBlack (T _ a y b) = T B a y b
makeBlack E = E

-- Tail-recursive insertion loop
buildTree :: Int -> Tree -> Tree
buildTree 0 acc = acc
buildTree n acc = buildTree (n - 1) (insert n acc)

-- Computes the maximum depth of the tree to force traversal
depth :: Tree -> Int
depth E = 0
depth (T _ a _ b) = 1 + max (depth a) (depth b)

max :: Int -> Int -> Int
max x y = if x > y then x else y

describe :: Effect Unit
describe = log "Red-Black Tree (100k Worst-Case Insertions):"

act :: Effect Int
act = do
  dummy <- Bench.opaque 100000
  pure ( depth (buildTree dummy E))

module Test.StateMonad where

import Prelude
import Effect (Effect)
import Effect.Console (log)
import Bench as Bench

-- A pure, custom implementation of the State Monad.
-- This relies purely on function closures rather than data structures.
newtype State s a = State (s -> { val :: a, state :: s })

runState :: forall s a. State s a -> s -> { val :: a, state :: s }
runState (State f) s = f s

-- The Bind operation creates a deeply nested closure
bindState :: forall s a b. State s a -> (a -> State s b) -> State s b
bindState (State f) g = State \s ->
  let r1 = f s
      State g' = g r1.val
  in g' r1.state

pureState :: forall s a. a -> State s a
pureState a = State \s -> { val: a, state: s }

get :: forall s. State s s
get = State \s -> { val: s, state: s }

put :: forall s. s -> State s Unit
put s = State \_ -> { val: unit, state: s }

modify :: forall s. (s -> s) -> State s Unit
modify f = bindState get \s -> put (f s)

-- Builds a chained sequence of State modifications.
-- Resolving this dives deep into the Call Stack (depth = n).
-- We cap n at 60 to avoid 'Maximum call stack size exceeded' in V8.
chainModifications :: Int -> State Int Unit
chainModifications 0 = pureState unit
chainModifications n = bindState (modify (\x -> x + 1)) \_ -> chainModifications (n - 1)

-- We run the 60-depth State monad 20 times to accumulate work.
-- Total: 1200 closures allocated and deeply evaluated.
runManyTimes :: Int -> Int -> Int
runManyTimes 0 acc = acc
runManyTimes n acc = runManyTimes (n - 1) (acc + (runState (chainModifications 60) 0).state)

describe :: Effect Unit
describe = log "State Monad (1.2k Binds, 60 Stack Depth):"

-- The result should be 20 * 60 = 1200
act :: Effect Int
act = do
  dummy <- Bench.opaque 20
  pure ( runManyTimes dummy 0)

module Test.LazyEvaluation where

import Prelude

import Effect (Effect)
import Effect.Console (log)
import Bench as Bench

newtype Lazy a = Lazy (Unit -> a)

defer :: forall a. (Unit -> a) -> Lazy a
defer = Lazy

force :: forall a. Lazy a -> a
force (Lazy f) = f unit

-- Builds a chain of n thunks.
-- When forced, it will consume n frames on the call stack.
-- Kept at 4000 to prevent V8 stack overflow (limit ~10400).
buildThunks :: Int -> Lazy Int -> Lazy Int
buildThunks 0 acc = acc
buildThunks n acc = buildThunks (n - 1) (defer \_ -> force acc + 1)

-- Evaluate the 1000-deep thunk chain 1000 times.
-- This allocates and evaluates 1 million thunks dynamically.
runManyTimes :: Int -> Int -> Int
runManyTimes 0 acc = acc
runManyTimes n acc = runManyTimes (n - 1) (acc + force (buildThunks 1000 (defer \_ -> 0)))

describe :: Effect Unit
describe = log "Lazy Evaluation (1M Thunks Forced, 1k Depth):"

-- The result should be 1000 * 1000 = 1000000
act :: Effect Int
act = do
  dummy <- Bench.opaque 1000
  pure ( runManyTimes dummy 0)

# Optimized imperative C reference

The main C column measures `bench_native.c`: an optimized imperative
implementation of the core workloads. Mutable data, native arrays, efficient
allocation and fused loops are allowed. It is not required to reproduce
PureScript's closures, dictionaries or persistent intermediate structures.
The separate functional C translation remains an archived experiment.

## Opaque inputs

The workload parameter must be obtained at run time on every timed invocation.
The compiler must not replace the input read with the literal used by the
benchmark driver, nor reuse an entire invocation's result across a batch.
The result is consumed, and expected values are verification data only.
This rule also applies to the other language columns; a source-level identity
function alone is not evidence that an optimizing compiler respects it.

Opacity does not forbid algebraic optimization of a function of its runtime
argument. For example, a loop may become a multiplication by the value just
read. It forbids replacing that value with the driver's known `1000` and
returning the precomputed answer. Multiple runtime inputs and inspection of
optimized output must distinguish these two situations.

Inputs and results follow the PureScript programs:

- AST: depth; build and evaluate the expression tree.
- Fibonacci: index; the recursive Fibonacci computation.
- List and Array: range endpoint; sum the even elements of the specified range.
  The array range descends when its endpoint is below its start; the custom
  list range is empty in that case.
- TCO: countdown; sum the remainders modulo three.
- Records: update count; compute the final nested field after the updates.
- Ackermann: first argument, with the second argument fixed at four.
- Church: base numeral; compute the composition's numeric result from it.
- Primes: upper bound; compute the prime sum.
- RBTree: descending insertion count; construct and balance the tree, then
  compute its depth. In-place Okasaki rotations are allowed; a formula returning
  the expected depth without constructing the tree is not a reference for this
  workload.
- Polymorphism: iteration count; compute the repeated integer operation.
- State: repetition count, with sixty state updates inside each repetition.
- Lazy: repetition count, with a chain depth of one thousand. An imperative
  computation may avoid materializing closures while computing the same value.
- RowToList: read the opaque value `10000`, then count the five-field record's
  keys. The PureScript source deliberately ignores that opaque value. A result
  independent of it is therefore expected; the count must come from the record
  structure, not a hard-coded oracle.

Integer operations preserve the Int32 results of the workloads without C
signed-overflow undefined behavior. Validation includes additional feasible
inputs, boundary cases and red-black-tree invariants, not just the fourteen
published answers.

## Timing and allocation

Construction, allocation and release of each invocation's working storage
belong to that timed invocation. There is no arena preallocated outside the
measurement or cached answer shared between calls. Stack storage and an arena
created within the invocation are legitimate imperative implementations.
This does not make C allocation and Go/JS garbage collection identical.

Build before measuring. Use a monotonic clock, three global warmups, three
local warmups, calibrated batches, the minimum of ten batches per process and
the median of three independent processes. Archive exact timings, inputs,
oracles, optimized-output checks, commands and source/executable hashes.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Measure frozen Go, official JS and a declared C core reference together.

Build all artifacts first. The C binary requires a build sidecar (by default
<binary>.manifest.json) with binary_sha256, source_sha256, toolchain, commands
and profile. This runner never compiles or republishes the historical catalogue.
"""
import argparse
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
from pathlib import Path
import platform
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
from measure import aggregate, check
from publish import ROWS, format_number, verify
from validate import CASES

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
C_REFERENCES = {
    'functional': {'backend': 'c-functional', 'label': 'C fonctionnel',
                   'source': 'tmp/bench_functional.c',
                   'contract': 'tmp/fp_reference_contract.md'},
    'imperative': {'backend': 'c-imperative', 'label': 'C impératif',
                   'source': 'tmp/bench_native.c',
                   'contract': 'tmp/imperative_reference_contract.md'},
}
BACKENDS = ('go', 'js', 'c-functional')
CORE_SOURCES = ['src/App.purs', 'src/Bench.purs'] + [
    f'src/Test/{module}/{module}.purs' for module in CASES]
PROTOCOL = {
    'processes_per_backend': 3, 'timed_batches_per_case': 10,
    'global_warmups': 3, 'local_warmups': 3,
    'calibration_target_ms': 10, 'maximum_batch_iterations': 16777216,
    'aggregation': 'median of the three process minima per case',
    'order': [list(BACKENDS[i:] + BACKENDS[:i]) for i in range(3)],
    'scope': '14 Stable core cases; no library or excluded diagnostics',
}


def c_reference(kind):
    if kind not in C_REFERENCES:
        raise ValueError(f'Unknown C reference kind: {kind}')
    return C_REFERENCES[kind]


def backends_for(kind):
    return ('go', 'js', c_reference(kind)['backend'])


def protocol_for(kind):
    backends = backends_for(kind)
    return {**PROTOCOL,
            'order': [list(backends[i:] + backends[:i]) for i in range(3)]}


def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def timestamp():
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


def load_average():
    return list(os.getloadavg()) if hasattr(os, 'getloadavg') else None


def json_file(path):
    return json.loads(Path(path).read_text())


def write_json(path, value):
    Path(path).write_text(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2,
                                    allow_nan=False) + '\n')


def verify_hashes(hashes, base=None):
    """Fail closed on changed/missing files, including build manifests."""
    for name, expected in hashes.items():
        path = Path(name) if base is None else Path(base) / name
        if not path.is_file() or sha(path) != expected:
            raise ValueError(f'Frozen input changed or is missing: {path}')


def verify_sources(directory, stored, names):
    for name in names:
        if name not in stored:
            raise ValueError(f'Build manifest omits source: {name}')
        verify_hashes({name: stored[name]}, ROOT)
        verify_hashes({name: stored[name]}, directory)


def inspect_go(directory):
    directory = Path(directory).resolve()
    path = directory / 'manifest.json'
    manifest = json_file(path)
    expected = {'language': 'go', 'mode': 'pure', 'test': None,
                'entry': 'App', 'include_library': False}
    if any(manifest.get(key) != value for key, value in expected.items()):
        raise ValueError('Expected a frozen Go App build containing exactly 14 core cases')
    profile = manifest['profile']
    if (profile.get('backend_profile') != 'release' or profile.get('pgo') is not False
            or str(profile.get('GOGC')) != '800'):
        raise ValueError('Go must be Release, GOGC=800, without PGO')
    names = CORE_SOURCES + ['src/Bench.go']
    verify_sources(directory, manifest['inputs'], names)
    binary = directory / 'benchmark'
    verify_hashes({str(binary): manifest['binary_sha256']})
    return {'manifest': manifest, 'manifest_path': str(path),
            'manifest_sha256': sha(path), 'command': [str(binary)],
            'cwd': str(directory), 'profile': profile,
            'toolchain': manifest['toolchain'],
            'payload_sha256': {str(binary): manifest['binary_sha256']},
            'source_sha256': {name: manifest['inputs'][name] for name in names}}


def js_payload(directory):
    output = Path(directory) / 'output'
    return {str(path.resolve()): sha(path) for path in sorted(output.rglob('*'))
            if path.is_file() and path.suffix in {'.js', '.json'}}


def inspect_js(directory):
    directory = Path(directory).resolve()
    path = directory / 'manifest.json'
    manifest = json_file(path)
    expected = {'backend': 'js', 'mode': 'pure', 'test': None,
                'entry': 'App', 'include_library': False}
    if any(manifest.get(key) != value for key, value in expected.items()):
        raise ValueError('Expected an official JavaScript App build with exactly 14 core cases')
    names = CORE_SOURCES + ['src/Bench.js']
    verify_sources(directory, manifest['source_sha256'], names)
    run = manifest['run']
    expected_run = ['node', '--input-type=module', '-e',
                    "import { main } from './output/App/index.js'; main();"]
    if run != expected_run:
        raise ValueError('Unexpected JavaScript runtime command; build the official App entry')
    node = shutil.which('node')
    if not node:
        raise ValueError('Node.js runtime is unavailable')
    node = str(Path(node).resolve())
    payload = js_payload(directory)
    if str(directory / 'output/App/index.js') not in payload:
        raise ValueError('JavaScript entry payload is missing')
    payload[node] = sha(node)
    compilers = [command[0] for command in manifest['commands']
                 if len(command) > 1 and command[1] == 'compile']
    if len(compilers) != 1:
        raise ValueError('Official PureScript compiler command is missing or ambiguous')
    compiler = str(Path(compilers[0]).resolve())
    compiler_version = subprocess.check_output([compiler, '--version'], text=True).strip()
    node_version = subprocess.check_output([node, '--version'], text=True).strip()
    return {'manifest': manifest, 'manifest_path': str(path),
            'manifest_sha256': sha(path), 'command': [node, *run[1:]],
            'cwd': str(directory), 'profile': {'compiler': 'official PureScript',
                                             'NODE_OPTIONS': os.environ.get('NODE_OPTIONS', '')},
            'toolchain': {'node': node_version, 'purescript': compiler_version,
                          'purescript_sha256': sha(compiler)},
            'payload_sha256': payload,
            'source_sha256': {name: manifest['source_sha256'][name] for name in names}}


def inspect_c(binary, manifest_path, source):
    binary, path, source = map(lambda p: Path(p).resolve(), (binary, manifest_path, source))
    manifest = json_file(path)
    source_name = str(source.relative_to(ROOT))
    if not manifest.get('commands') or not manifest.get('toolchain') or not manifest.get('profile'):
        raise ValueError('C build manifest must record commands, toolchain and profile')
    if source_name not in manifest.get('source_sha256', {}):
        raise ValueError(f'C build manifest omits {source_name}')
    verify_hashes(manifest['source_sha256'], ROOT)
    verify_hashes({str(binary): manifest['binary_sha256']})
    return {'manifest': manifest, 'manifest_path': str(path),
            'manifest_sha256': sha(path), 'command': [str(binary)],
            'cwd': str(binary.parent), 'profile': manifest['profile'],
            'toolchain': manifest['toolchain'],
            'payload_sha256': {str(binary): manifest['binary_sha256']},
            'source_sha256': manifest['source_sha256']}


def source_snapshot(c_source, c_kind='functional'):
    names = CORE_SOURCES + ['src/Bench.go', 'src/Bench.js',
                           str(Path(c_source).resolve().relative_to(ROOT)),
                           c_reference(c_kind)['contract'],
                           'bin/benchmark/compare-core.py', 'bin/benchmark/measure.py',
                           'bin/benchmark/validate.py', 'bin/benchmark/publish.py']
    catalogue = ROOT / 'bin/benchmark/ratio-measurements.json'
    if catalogue.is_file():
        names.append(str(catalogue.relative_to(ROOT)))
    return {name: sha(ROOT / name) for name in names}


def verify_frozen(builds, sources):
    verify_hashes(sources, ROOT)
    for key, build in builds.items():
        verify_hashes({build['manifest_path']: build['manifest_sha256']})
        verify_hashes(build['payload_sha256'])
        if key == 'js':
            current = js_payload(build['cwd'])
            expected = {name: value for name, value in build['payload_sha256'].items()
                        if Path(name).is_relative_to(Path(build['cwd']).resolve() / 'output')}
            if current != expected:
                raise ValueError('JavaScript payload inventory changed during the campaign')


def check_core(output):
    checked = check(output, 'pure')
    if 'library' in checked or len(checked['times_us']) != 14:
        raise ValueError('This comparison requires exactly 14 core cases')
    return checked


def rankings(results, c_kind='functional'):
    c_backend = c_reference(c_kind)['backend']
    if set(results) != set(backends_for(c_kind)):
        raise ValueError('All three complete backend columns are required')
    for key, result in results.items():
        verify(key, result)
    rows = []
    for index, (name, module) in enumerate(zip(ROWS, CASES)):
        times = {key: result['times_us'][index] for key, result in results.items()}
        samples = {key: [sample['times_us'][index] for sample in result['process_runs']]
                   for key, result in results.items()}
        variability = {}
        for reference, key in [(c_backend, 'go_c'), ('js', 'go_js')]:
            ratios = [go / other for go, other in zip(samples['go'], samples[reference])]
            variability[key] = {'ratios_by_cycle': ratios, 'minimum': min(ratios),
                                'maximum': max(ratios),
                                'interpretation': 'Observed ratios within each rotating cycle; '
                                                  'not a confidence interval.'}
        rows.append({'case': name, 'module': f'Test.{module}',
                     'label': results['go']['labels'][index],
                     'expected': results['go']['values'][index], 'times_us': times,
                     'process_samples_us': samples, 'ratio_variability': variability,
                     'go_over_c': times['go'] / times[c_backend],
                     'go_over_js': times['go'] / times['js']})
    return {'go_c': sorted(rows, key=lambda row: (-row['go_over_c'], row['case'])),
            'go_js': sorted(rows, key=lambda row: (-row['go_over_js'], row['case']))}


def historical_comparison(results):
    path = ROOT / 'bin/benchmark/ratio-measurements.json'
    if not path.is_file():
        return None
    catalogue = json_file(path)
    columns = catalogue.get('columns', {})
    rows = []
    for index, name in enumerate(ROWS):
        old = {key: columns.get(key, {}).get(name) for key in ['go-pure', 'js-pure', 'c']}
        values = {}
        for old_key, fresh_key in [('go-pure', 'go'), ('js-pure', 'js')]:
            item = old[old_key]
            if item and math.isfinite(item['time_us']) and item['time_us'] > 0:
                values[fresh_key] = {'archived': item,
                                    'fresh_over_archived': results[fresh_key]['times_us'][index] / item['time_us']}
        rows.append({'case': name, 'program_timings': values,
                     'c_archived': old['c']})
    return {'catalogue': str(path.relative_to(ROOT)), 'sha256': sha(path),
            'note': 'Historical observations only, not paired measurements. '
                    'Archived C timings retain their recorded source identity; '
                    'they may describe a different C implementation.',
            'cases': rows}


def render_report(report):
    kind = report.get('c_reference', {}).get('kind', 'functional')
    reference = c_reference(kind)
    if kind == 'functional':
        scope = ('La référence C traduit la structure fonctionnelle des cas. Les backends restent libres '
                 'd’optimiser : une forme close légitime est un résultat de compilation, pas une erreur. ')
        memory = ('Le C alloue via `malloc` avec un registre et libère les allocations dans chaque action '
                  'chronométrée ; aucune arène préallouée hors mesure n’est utilisée. ')
        verification = ('La correction des oracles ne prouve pas à elle seule '
                        'l’équivalence structurelle : le contrat et le source C doivent être lus avec ces résultats.')
    else:
        scope = ('La référence C est impérative et optimisée. Ses algorithmes et structures mutables '
                 'peuvent différer de ceux des sources PureScript, avec les mêmes entrées et résultats. '
                 'Les entrées restent opaques à l’optimisation ; les simplifications algébriques '
                 'qui calculent encore le résultat depuis l’entrée d’exécution restent permises. ')
        memory = ('Les allocations et libérations nécessaires au C sont incluses dans chaque action '
                  'chronométrée ; aucune arène préallouée hors mesure n’est utilisée. ')
        verification = ('Les oracles ne prouvent pas à eux seuls l’opacité des entrées ni '
                        'l’équivalence pour d’autres paramètres : le contrat, les vérifications '
                        'complémentaires et le source C doivent être lus avec ces résultats.')
    lines = [f"# Comparaison des 14 cas : Go, JavaScript officiel et {reference['label']}", '',
             f"Campagne terminée : {report['completed_at_utc']} (UTC).", '',
             'Les ratios sont les temps Go divisés par la référence : au-dessus de 1×, Go est plus lent. '
             'Le tri utilise les valeurs archivées avant arrondi. Les deux classements couvrent 14/14 cas.', '',
             '## Protocole', '',
             'Trois processus indépendants par backend, ordre tournant Go/JS/C, JS/C/Go, C/Go/JS. '
             'Trois échauffements globaux et locaux, calibration vers 10 ms, dix batches ; '
             'chaque durée publiée est la médiane des trois minima par processus. '
             'Tous les résultats et tailles de batches ont passé le validateur commun. '
             'Les sources et artefacts ont été figés et vérifiés avant et après chaque exécution.', '',
             'Go : Release, GOGC=800, sans PGO, GOMAXPROCS par défaut. '
             'JavaScript : compilateur PureScript officiel, runtime Node.js. '
             f"C : référence {('fonctionnelle' if kind == 'functional' else 'impérative')} "
             'compilée séparément avant la campagne. '
             'Les versions, commandes, profils, hashes, labels/paramètres, oracles et sorties brutes '
             'sont archivés dans `results.json` et `manifest.json`. Les sources mesurées et le contrat '
             'C sont copiés sous `sources/`.', '',
             'La machine n’est pas isolée des autres activités. La charge système au début et à la fin '
             'de chaque processus est archivée. Les intervalles min–max ci-dessous sont les ratios '
             'observés dans les trois cycles tournants, pas des intervalles de confiance. '
             'Le classement porte sur les ratios des médianes, qui peuvent différer de la médiane '
             'des ratios par cycle.', '',
             '## Portée de la comparaison', '',
             scope +
             'Ces ratios comparent les programmes complets optimisés ; ils ne sont pas des coûts '
             'par opération source ni la preuve d’un nombre identique d’opérations machine.', '',
             memory +
             'Go et JavaScript utilisent leur GC. '
             'Les représentations et coûts de libération restent donc différents. '
             'Les trois harnais consomment les résultats via des accès atomiques ; les instructions '
             'natives et les adaptations FFI Go/JS restent différentes. '
             'Les adaptations d’appel et harnais sont incluses ; les très petits temps peuvent '
             'être dominés par ces coûts. ' + verification, '']
    for title, key, backend, ratio in [(f"Go / {reference['label']}", 'go_c', reference['backend'], 'go_over_c'),
                                      ('Go / JavaScript officiel', 'go_js', 'js', 'go_over_js')]:
        lines += [f'## {title} — ordre décroissant', '',
                  '| Cas | Go (µs) | Référence (µs) | Ratio | Min–max des ratios par cycle |',
                  '| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |']
        for row in report['rankings'][key]:
            spread = row['ratio_variability'][key]
            lines.append(f"| {row['case']} | {format_number(row['times_us']['go'])} | "
                         f"{format_number(row['times_us'][backend])} | {format_number(row[ratio])}× | "
                         f"{format_number(spread['minimum'])}–{format_number(spread['maximum'])}× |")
        lines += ['']
    history = report.get('historical_comparison')
    if history:
        lines += ['## Baselines historiques — comparaison séparée', '',
                  'Le catalogue reste inchangé par cette collecte. La référence C archivée garde '
                  'son identité et sa provenance ; elle peut différer de celle de cette campagne. Les variations suivantes '
                  'confrontent les mesures Go/JS fraîches aux baselines archivées du README ; '
                  'elles ne sont pas une expérience avant/après appariée et peuvent inclure des '
                  'changements de harnais, versions ou environnement.', '',
                  '| Cas | Go frais / Go archivé | JS frais / JS archivé | C archivé (µs) |',
                  '| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |']
        for row in history['cases']:
            values = row['program_timings']
            cells = [format_number(values[key]['fresh_over_archived']) + '×' if key in values else '—'
                     for key in ['go', 'js']]
            old_c = row.get('c_archived', row.get('imperative_c_archived'))
            cells.append(format_number(old_c['time_us']) if old_c else '—')
            lines.append('| ' + row['case'] + ' | ' + ' | '.join(cells) + ' |')
        lines += ['']
    return '\n'.join(lines)


def run_campaign(builds, output, sources, timeout, c_kind='functional'):
    backends = backends_for(c_kind)
    protocol = protocol_for(c_kind)
    if set(builds) != set(backends):
        raise ValueError('Build identities do not match the declared C reference kind')
    output = Path(output).resolve()
    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    verify_hashes(sources, ROOT)
    for name in sources:
        destination = output / 'sources' / name
        destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copyfile(ROOT / name, destination)
    verify_hashes(sources, output / 'sources')
    env = dict(os.environ, GOGC='800')
    env.pop('GOMAXPROCS', None)
    env.pop('PPROF', None)
    manifest = {'started_at_utc': timestamp(), 'host': platform.platform(),
                'machine': platform.machine(), 'protocol': protocol,
                'c_reference': {'kind': c_kind, 'backend': c_reference(c_kind)['backend'],
                                'contract': c_reference(c_kind)['contract']},
                'load_average_start': load_average(), 'host_isolated': False,
                'environment': {name: env.get(name, 'unset') for name in
                                ['GOGC', 'GOMAXPROCS', 'GOMEMLIMIT', 'GODEBUG', 'NODE_OPTIONS']},
                'sources_sha256': sources, 'builds': builds, 'runs': []}
    write_json(output / 'manifest.json', manifest)
    samples = {key: [] for key in backends}
    for cycle, order in enumerate(protocol['order'], 1):
        for key in order:
            verify_frozen(builds, sources)
            build = builds[key]
            stem = f'{cycle}-{key}'
            started = timestamp()
            load_start = load_average()
            print(f'Measuring {key}: process {cycle}/3', flush=True)
            with (output / f'{stem}.stdout').open('w') as out, (output / f'{stem}.stderr').open('w') as err:
                process = subprocess.run(build['command'], cwd=build['cwd'], env=env,
                                         stdout=out, stderr=err, timeout=timeout)
            process.check_returncode()
            load_end = load_average()
            verify_frozen(builds, sources)
            raw = (output / f'{stem}.stdout').read_text()
            checked = check_core(raw)
            write_json(output / f'{stem}.json', checked)
            samples[key].append(checked)
            manifest['runs'].append({'backend': key, 'process': cycle,
                                     'started_at_utc': started, 'completed_at_utc': timestamp(),
                                     'load_average_start': load_start, 'load_average_end': load_end,
                                     'command': build['command'], 'cwd': build['cwd'],
                                     'files_sha256': {f'{stem}.{suffix}': sha(output / f'{stem}.{suffix}')
                                                      for suffix in ['stdout', 'stderr', 'json']}})
            write_json(output / 'manifest.json', manifest)
            print(f'{stem}: 14 oracles and calibrated batches verified', flush=True)
    results = {key: aggregate(values) for key, values in samples.items()}
    report = {'started_at_utc': manifest['started_at_utc'], 'completed_at_utc': timestamp(),
              'scope': {'core_cases': 14, 'backends': list(backends)},
              'c_reference': manifest['c_reference'],
              'protocol': protocol, 'environment': manifest['environment'],
              'host': manifest['host'], 'machine': manifest['machine'], 'host_isolated': False,
              'load_average_start': manifest['load_average_start'], 'load_average_end': load_average(),
              'runs': manifest['runs'],
              'sources_sha256': sources, 'builds': builds, 'results': results,
              'rankings': rankings(results, c_kind), 'historical_comparison': historical_comparison(results)}
    verify_frozen(builds, sources)
    write_json(output / 'results.json', report)
    (output / 'report.md').write_text(render_report(report))
    manifest['completed_at_utc'] = report['completed_at_utc']
    manifest['load_average_end'] = report['load_average_end']
    manifest['results_sha256'] = sha(output / 'results.json')
    manifest['report_sha256'] = sha(output / 'report.md')
    write_json(output / 'manifest.json', manifest)
    print(f'Complete comparison: {output / "report.md"}', flush=True)
    return report


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--go-dir', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--js-dir', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--c-binary', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--c-manifest', type=Path)
    parser.add_argument('--c-kind', choices=tuple(C_REFERENCES), default='functional',
                        help='C implementation identity (default: functional)')
    parser.add_argument('--c-source', type=Path,
                        help='defaults to bench_functional.c or bench_native.c according to --c-kind')
    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--timeout', type=float, default=600)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    c_source = args.c_source or ROOT / c_reference(args.c_kind)['source']
    c_backend = c_reference(args.c_kind)['backend']
    c_manifest = args.c_manifest or Path(str(args.c_binary) + '.manifest.json')
    builds = {'go': inspect_go(args.go_dir), 'js': inspect_js(args.js_dir),
              c_backend: inspect_c(args.c_binary, c_manifest, c_source)}
    for name in CORE_SOURCES:
        if builds['go']['source_sha256'][name] != builds['js']['source_sha256'][name]:
            raise ValueError(f'Go and JS do not share the same PureScript source: {name}')
    sources = source_snapshot(c_source, args.c_kind)
    verify_frozen(builds, sources)
    run_campaign(builds, args.output, sources, args.timeout, args.c_kind)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    try:
        main()
    except (ValueError, OSError, KeyError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as error:
        print(f'ERROR: {error}', file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Validate benchmark results and timings, forwarding stdin unchanged."""
import argparse
import json
import math
from pathlib import Path
import re
import runpy
import sys

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
LIBRARY_MARKER = "=== Excluded WIP benchmarks ==="
CASES = dict(zip(
    ["AstTree", "Fib", "ListOps", "TCO", "Records", "Ackermann", "Church",
     "Primes", "RBTree", "Polymorphism", "StateMonad", "LazyEvaluation", "ArrayOps", "RowToList"],
    ["7", "55", "202950", "100000", "20000", "125", "100000", "21536",
     "22", "10000000", "1200", "1000000", "202950", "5"]))
ROW = re.compile(
    r"\(Test\)\s*\n\s*([^\n]+)\s*\n\s*\(Output & Warm-up\)\s*\n"
    r"(.*?)\(Execution time - best of 10\)\s*\n\s*(\S+)\s+μs", re.S)
EXTENDED_CASES = [
    {"module": "Test.FileOps", "label": "File I/O (10k writes/reads):", "value": "10000"},
    {"module": "Test.STArray", "label": "STArray Operations:", "value": "10"},
    {"module": "Test.StringOps", "label": "String Operations (1k Regex/Split):", "value": "2000"},
    # Timer APIs can round a 10 ms deadline to their millisecond clock tick.
    # Allow one tick, while rejecting a no-op delay with the correct text output.
    {"module": "Test.AffOperations", "label": "Aff Operations (Asynchronous Delays)",
     "value": "10", "minimum_us": 9000.0},
    {"module": "Test.Parallelism", "label": "Parallelism (10 x Fib 42)",
     "value": "Checksum: 679142946"},
]


def case_for(module, expected=None):
    name = module.removeprefix("Test.")
    base = name.removesuffix("FFICheatcode").removesuffix("FFI")
    value = CASES.get(base) if expected is None else expected
    if value is None:
        raise ValueError(f"No core oracle for {module}; supply --expected VALUE for a custom --test")
    source = ROOT / "src/Test" / base.replace(".", "/") / (name.rsplit(".", 1)[-1] + ".purs")
    if not source.is_file():
        raise ValueError(f"Missing source for {module}: {source}")
    label = re.search(r'(?m)^describe\s*=\s*(?:\w+\.)?log\s+"([^"\n]+)"', source.read_text())
    if not label:
        raise ValueError(f"Cannot find literal benchmark label in {source}")
    return {"module": "Test." + name, "label": label.group(1), "value": str(value)}


def expected_cases(mode, test=None, expected=None):
    if mode == "test":
        if not test or not re.fullmatch(r"(?:Test\.)?[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_.]*", test):
            raise ValueError("--mode test requires a valid --test MODULE")
        return [case_for(test, expected)]
    if expected is not None or test:
        raise ValueError("--test and --expected require --mode test")
    if mode == "x":
        return [dict(case) for case in EXTENDED_CASES]
    if mode == "wip":
        # Some backend runners load this validator by filename without adding
        # its directory to sys.path. Keep the WIP section equally portable.
        suite = runpy.run_path(str(ROOT / "bin/benchmark/library_suite.py"))
        return suite["library_cases"]()
    if mode not in {"pure", "ffi", "fficc"}:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown benchmark mode {mode}")
    suffix = {"pure": "", "ffi": "FFI", "fficc": "FFICheatcode"}[mode]
    return [case_for(name + suffix) for name in CASES]


def split_library_output(output):
    """Split the appended section, preserving older core-only log support."""
    markers = list(re.finditer(r"(?m)^" + re.escape(LIBRARY_MARKER) + r"\r?$", output))
    if len(markers) > 1 or output.count(LIBRARY_MARKER) != len(markers):
        raise ValueError("Repeated or malformed WIP benchmark marker")
    if not markers:
        return output, None
    marker = markers[0]
    return output[:marker.start()], output[marker.end():]


def validate_section(output, mode, test=None, expected=None):
    """Validate one core/extended section or the excluded WIP section."""
    cases = expected_cases(mode, test, expected)
    rows = ROW.findall(output)
    if (len(rows) != len(cases) or output.count("(Test)") != len(cases)
            or output.count("(Output & Warm-up)") != len(cases)
            or output.count("(Execution time - best of 10)") != len(cases)):
        raise ValueError(f"Expected exactly {len(cases)} complete benchmark rows; found {len(rows)}")
    times, values, labels = [], [], []
    for (label, value, elapsed), case in zip(rows, cases):
        label, value = label.strip(), value.strip()
        if label != case["label"]:
            raise ValueError(f"Unexpected benchmark label {label!r}; expected {case['label']!r}")
        if case["value"] is not None and value != case["value"]:
            raise ValueError(f"{label} returned {value!r}; expected {case['value']!r}")
        duration = float(elapsed)
        if not math.isfinite(duration) or duration < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid duration for {label}: {elapsed}")
        if duration < case.get("minimum_us", 0):
            raise ValueError(f"{label} completed in {duration} μs; expected the 10 ms timer to elapse")
        labels.append(label)
        values.append(value)
        times.append(duration)
    totals = re.findall(r"Total exec time:\s*(\S+)\s+ms", output)
    if len(totals) != (0 if mode in {"test", "wip"} else 1):
        raise ValueError("Missing or repeated benchmark total")
    summed = sum(times) / 1000.0
    # At most .005 μs rounding per row and .005 ms for the printed total.
    tolerance = .005 + len(rows) * .005 / 1000 + 1e-8
    total = float(totals[0]) if totals else None
    if total is not None and (not math.isfinite(total) or total < 0 or abs(total - summed) > tolerance):
        raise ValueError(f"Printed total {total} ms differs from row sum {summed} ms")
    return {"mode": mode, "labels": labels, "values": values, "times_us": times,
            "total_ms": total, "sum_displayed_lines_ms": None if mode == "wip" else summed,
            "values_validated": True,
            "oracle": "wip" if mode == "wip" else "extended" if mode == "x" else "core",
            "timer_unit": "microseconds"}


def validate_output(output, mode="pure", test=None, expected=None, include_library=False):
    if mode not in {"pure", "ffi", "fficc", "test", "x", "wip"}:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown benchmark mode {mode}")
    core_output, library_output = split_library_output(output)
    if mode not in {"pure", "ffi", "fficc"} and (include_library or library_output is not None):
        raise ValueError("An appended WIP section is only valid after a core suite")
    if include_library and library_output is None:
        raise ValueError("Missing excluded WIP benchmark section")
    result = validate_section(core_output, mode, test, expected)
    if library_output is not None:
        result["library"] = validate_section(library_output, "wip")
    return result


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--mode", choices=["pure", "ffi", "fficc", "test", "x", "wip"], default="pure")
    parser.add_argument("--test")
    parser.add_argument("--expected")
    parser.add_argument("--input", type=Path, help="read an existing log instead of stdin")
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, help="write validated results as JSON")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    chunks = []
    source = args.input.open() if args.input else sys.stdin
    try:
        for line in source:
            chunks.append(line)
            print(line, end="", flush=True)
        result = validate_output("".join(chunks), args.mode, args.test, args.expected)
        if args.output:
            args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            args.output.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
        message = f"{len(result['values'])} expected {result['oracle']} results and timings verified"
        if "library" in result:
            message += f"; {len(result['library']['values'])} excluded WIP results and timings verified"
        print("Benchmark validation: " + message, file=sys.stderr)
    except (ValueError, OSError) as error:
        print("Benchmark validation failed: " + str(error), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    finally:
        if args.input:
            source.close()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check core comparison provenance, complete oracles and unrounded rankings."""
import copy
import json
from pathlib import Path
import runpy
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from unittest.mock import patch

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark'))
C = runpy.run_path(str(ROOT / 'bin/benchmark/compare-core.py'))
from measure import aggregate
from validate import expected_cases


def output_fixture(times=None):
    cases = expected_cases('pure')
    times = [1.0] * 14 if times is None else times
    rows = []
    for case, elapsed in zip(cases, times):
        rows.append(f"(Test)\n{case['label']}\n\n(Output & Warm-up)\n{case['value']}\n\n"
                    f"(Execution time - best of 10)\n\n{elapsed:.9f} μs\n\nBatch iterations: 1024\n")
    return '\n'.join(rows) + f'\nTotal exec time: {sum(times) / 1000:.9f} ms\n'


def column(times=None):
    checked = C['check_core'](output_fixture(times))
    return aggregate([copy.deepcopy(checked) for _ in range(3)])


class CoreComparison(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_fourteen_oracles_and_calibrated_batches_are_required(self):
        valid = output_fixture()
        self.assertEqual(len(C['check_core'](valid)['times_us']), 14)
        invalid = [valid.replace('(Output & Warm-up)\n7\n', '(Output & Warm-up)\n8\n', 1),
                   valid.replace('Batch iterations: 1024', 'Batch iterations: 1023', 1),
                   valid.replace('1.000000000 μs', '0.000000000 μs', 1),
                   output_fixture([1.0] * 13)]
        for text in invalid:
            with self.subTest(text=text[:50]), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                C['check_core'](text)

    def test_rankings_use_raw_ratios_before_rounding(self):
        go = [1.0] * 14
        go[0], go[1] = 1.00001, 1.00002
        result = C['rankings']({'go': column(go), 'js': column([2.0] * 14),
                                'c-functional': column()})
        for key in ['go_c', 'go_js']:
            self.assertEqual(len(result[key]), 14)
            self.assertEqual([row['case'] for row in result[key][:2]], ['Fibonacci', 'AST Evaluation'])
        self.assertEqual(result['go_c'][0]['go_over_c'], 1.00002)
        self.assertEqual(result['go_js'][0]['go_over_js'], 0.50001)
        self.assertEqual(result['go_js'][0]['expected'], '55')

    def test_ratios_use_medians_and_preserve_variability_separately(self):
        values = {}
        for key, samples in {'go': [1, 6, 10], 'js': [1, 10, 3],
                             'c-functional': [2, 4, 5]}.items():
            values[key] = aggregate([C['check_core'](output_fixture([float(t)] * 14)) for t in samples])
        row = C['rankings'](values)['go_js'][0]
        self.assertEqual(row['go_over_js'], 2.0)  # median(1,6,10) / median(1,10,3)
        spread = row['ratio_variability']['go_js']
        self.assertEqual(spread['ratios_by_cycle'], [1.0, 0.6, 10 / 3])
        self.assertEqual(spread['minimum'], 0.6)
        self.assertEqual(spread['maximum'], 10 / 3)

    def test_imperative_rankings_require_and_retain_the_declared_identity(self):
        results = {'go': column([6.0] * 14), 'js': column([3.0] * 14),
                   'c-imperative': column([2.0] * 14)}
        rows = C['rankings'](results, 'imperative')
        row = rows['go_c'][0]
        self.assertEqual(row['go_over_c'], 3)
        self.assertEqual(row['go_over_js'], 2)
        self.assertEqual(row['times_us']['c-imperative'], 2)
        self.assertNotIn('c-functional', row['times_us'])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            C['rankings'](results)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            C['rankings']({**results, 'c-functional': column()}, 'imperative')

    def test_snapshot_freezes_the_selected_contract_and_shared_opaque_boundaries(self):
        globals_ = C['source_snapshot'].__globals__
        with patch.dict(globals_, sha=lambda path: str(path)):
            for kind, source, contract in [
                    ('functional', 'tmp/bench_functional.c', 'tmp/fp_reference_contract.md'),
                    ('imperative', 'tmp/bench_native.c', 'tmp/imperative_reference_contract.md')]:
                with self.subTest(kind=kind):
                    snapshot = C['source_snapshot'](ROOT / source, kind)
                    self.assertIn(source, snapshot)
                    self.assertIn(contract, snapshot)
                    self.assertIn('src/Bench.purs', snapshot)
                    self.assertIn('src/Bench.go', snapshot)
                    self.assertIn('src/Bench.js', snapshot)
                    other = ('tmp/fp_reference_contract.md' if kind == 'imperative'
                             else 'tmp/imperative_reference_contract.md')
                    self.assertNotIn(other, snapshot)

    def test_historical_c_keeps_provenance_without_assuming_an_implementation(self):
        stored = {'time_us': 7.0, 'source': 'archived-functional.json'}
        catalogue = {'columns': {'c': {name: stored for name in C['ROWS']}}}
        globals_ = C['historical_comparison'].__globals__
        with patch.dict(globals_, json_file=lambda _: catalogue, sha=lambda _: 'digest'):
            history = C['historical_comparison']({'go': column(), 'js': column()})
        self.assertEqual(history['cases'][0]['c_archived'], stored)
        self.assertNotIn('imperative_c_archived', history['cases'][0])
        self.assertIn('recorded source identity', history['note'])

    def test_partial_columns_or_tampered_aggregate_are_rejected(self):
        results = {key: column() for key in C['BACKENDS']}
        mutations = [lambda r: r.pop('js'),
                     lambda r: r['go']['times_us'].pop(),
                     lambda r: r['go']['values'].__setitem__(0, 'wrong'),
                     lambda r: r['go']['times_us'].__setitem__(0, 9.0),
                     lambda r: r['go']['process_runs'].pop()]
        for mutation in mutations:
            changed = copy.deepcopy(results)
            mutation(changed)
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                C['rankings'](changed)

    def test_hashes_reject_changed_and_missing_files(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            path = Path(temporary) / 'artifact'
            path.write_bytes(b'frozen')
            hashes = {str(path): C['sha'](path)}
            C['verify_hashes'](hashes)
            path.write_bytes(b'changed')
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'Frozen input changed'):
                C['verify_hashes'](hashes)
            path.unlink()
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'missing'):
                C['verify_hashes'](hashes)

    def test_js_payload_new_file_invalidates_frozen_inventory(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            directory = Path(temporary)
            output = directory / 'output/App'
            output.mkdir(parents=True)
            (output / 'index.js').write_text('export const main = () => {};')
            manifest = directory / 'manifest.json'
            manifest.write_text('{}')
            builds = {'js': {'manifest_path': str(manifest), 'manifest_sha256': C['sha'](manifest),
                             'cwd': str(directory), 'payload_sha256': C['js_payload'](directory)}}
            C['verify_frozen'](builds, {})
            (output / 'foreign.js').write_text('export const extra = 1;')
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'inventory changed'):
                C['verify_frozen'](builds, {})

    def test_c_binary_must_match_its_build_manifest(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT / 'tmp') as temporary:
            directory = Path(temporary)
            source, binary = directory / 'reference.c', directory / 'reference'
            source.write_text('int main(void) { return 0; }')
            binary.write_bytes(b'compiled-placeholder')
            manifest = directory / 'reference.manifest.json'
            manifest.write_text(json.dumps({'binary_sha256': C['sha'](binary),
                'source_sha256': {str(source.relative_to(ROOT)): C['sha'](source)},
                'commands': [['clang', '-O3', str(source)]],
                'toolchain': 'test compiler', 'profile': {'optimization': '-O3'}}))
            C['inspect_c'](binary, manifest, source)
            source.write_text('int main(void) { return 1; }')
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'Frozen input changed'):
                C['inspect_c'](binary, manifest, source)

    def test_three_rotating_processes_archive_reports_without_publication(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            output = Path(temporary) / 'campaign'
            builds = {key: {'command': [key], 'cwd': temporary} for key in C['BACKENDS']}
            seen = []

            def fake_run(command, **kwargs):
                seen.append(command[0])
                kwargs['stdout'].write(output_fixture())
                return subprocess.CompletedProcess(command, 0)

            # Simulate only execution; freeze checks have independent mutation tests.
            globals_ = C['run_campaign'].__globals__
            with patch.dict(globals_, verify_frozen=lambda *_: None,
                            historical_comparison=lambda _: None), \
                    patch.object(C['platform'], 'platform', return_value='test host'), \
                    patch.object(subprocess, 'run', side_effect=fake_run):
                report = C['run_campaign'](builds, output, {}, 5)
            self.assertEqual(seen, ['go', 'js', 'c-functional', 'js', 'c-functional', 'go',
                                    'c-functional', 'go', 'js'])
            self.assertEqual(len(report['runs']), 9)
            self.assertFalse(report['host_isolated'])
            self.assertTrue(all(len(result['process_runs']) == 3 for result in report['results'].values()))
            manifest = json.loads((output / 'manifest.json').read_text())
            self.assertEqual(manifest['results_sha256'], C['sha'](output / 'results.json'))
            self.assertEqual(manifest['report_sha256'], C['sha'](output / 'report.md'))
            self.assertEqual(len(list(output.glob('*.stdout'))), 9)
            self.assertEqual(len(list(output.glob('*.stderr'))), 9)
            self.assertIn('14/14', (output / 'report.md').read_text())
            with self.assertRaises(FileExistsError):
                C['run_campaign'](builds, output, {}, 5)

    def test_imperative_campaign_archives_its_own_identity_and_protocol(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            output = Path(temporary) / 'imperative'
            builds = {key: {'command': [key], 'cwd': temporary}
                      for key in ('go', 'js', 'c-imperative')}
            seen = []

            def fake_run(command, **kwargs):
                seen.append(command[0])
                kwargs['stdout'].write(output_fixture())
                return subprocess.CompletedProcess(command, 0)

            globals_ = C['run_campaign'].__globals__
            with patch.dict(globals_, verify_frozen=lambda *_: None,
                            historical_comparison=lambda _: None), \
                    patch.object(C['platform'], 'platform', return_value='test host'), \
                    patch.object(subprocess, 'run', side_effect=fake_run):
                report = C['run_campaign'](builds, output, {}, 5, 'imperative')
            self.assertEqual(seen, ['go', 'js', 'c-imperative', 'js', 'c-imperative', 'go',
                                    'c-imperative', 'go', 'js'])
            self.assertEqual(report['c_reference'], {
                'kind': 'imperative', 'backend': 'c-imperative',
                'contract': 'tmp/imperative_reference_contract.md'})
            manifest = json.loads((output / 'manifest.json').read_text())
            self.assertEqual(manifest['c_reference'], report['c_reference'])
            self.assertEqual(report['scope']['backends'], ['go', 'js', 'c-imperative'])
            self.assertNotIn('c-functional', report['results'])
            text = (output / 'report.md').read_text()
            self.assertIn('Go / C impératif', text)
            self.assertIn('entrées restent opaques', text)
            self.assertNotIn('C fonctionnel', text)
            self.assertNotIn('malloc` avec un registre', text)
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'Build identities'):
                C['run_campaign'](builds, output / 'wrong-kind', {}, 5)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compile the imperative reference and vary inputs after compilation."""
import os
from pathlib import Path
import random
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SOURCE = ROOT / 'tmp/bench_native.c'


class ImperativeReference(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.compiler = shutil.which('clang')
        if not cls.compiler:
            raise unittest.SkipTest('clang is required for the native reference')
        cls.workspace = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='altbak-imperative-reference-')
        cls.binary = Path(cls.workspace.name) / 'reference'
        subprocess.run([cls.compiler, '-std=c11', '-O3', '-Wall', '-Wextra', '-Werror',
                        str(SOURCE), '-o', str(cls.binary)], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True)

    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls):
        cls.workspace.cleanup()

    def run_case(self, name, value):
        return int(subprocess.check_output([str(self.binary), '--case', name, str(value)], text=True))

    def test_all_benchmark_oracles_variants_and_tree_invariants(self):
        result = subprocess.check_output([str(self.binary), '--verify'], text=True)
        self.assertIn('14 core oracles, 56 input variants, 257 tree sizes', result)
        self.assertIn('rotations, duplicates and Int32 arithmetic', result)

    def test_inputs_are_selected_after_compilation(self):
        # These values enter through argv, after the optimized executable exists.
        # Arithmetic simplification is valid; substituting the benchmark's fixed
        # expected result is not.
        values = [0, 1, 2, 17] + random.Random(8217).sample(range(3, 300), 5)
        for value in values:
            for case, expected in [
                ('Polymorphism', value), ('StateMonad', value * 60),
                ('LazyEvaluation', value * 1000),
                ('ListOps', sum(i for i in range(1, value + 1) if i % 2 == 0)),
                ('TCO', sum(i % 3 for i in range(1, value + 1))),
                ('Records', sum(i % 5 for i in range(1, value + 1))),
            ]:
                with self.subTest(case=case, value=value):
                    self.assertEqual(self.run_case(case, value), expected)
        for value in range(-11, 12):
            step = 1 if value >= 1 else -1
            expected = sum(i for i in range(1, value + step, step) if i % 2 == 0)
            self.assertEqual(self.run_case('ArrayOps', value), expected)
        for value in range(7):
            self.assertEqual(self.run_case('Church', value), value ** 5)
        # The source deliberately ignores its opaque number and counts a fixed
        # record's fields. That input-independent result is part of its contract.
        for value in [-2147483648, -1, 0, 17, 10000, 2147483647]:
            self.assertEqual(self.run_case('RowToList', value), 5)

    def test_invalid_inputs_are_rejected_instead_of_returning_a_guess(self):
        for case, value in [('AstTree', -1), ('AstTree', 13), ('Ackermann', 4),
                            ('Fib', 'abc'), ('RowToList', 2147483648), ('unknown', 1)]:
            result = subprocess.run([str(self.binary), '--case', case, str(value)],
                                    text=True, capture_output=True)
            self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 2, (case, value, result))

    def test_sanitized_oracles_and_mutable_tree(self):
        binary = Path(self.workspace.name) / 'reference-sanitized'
        subprocess.run([self.compiler, '-std=c11', '-O1', '-g', '-Wall', '-Wextra', '-Werror',
                        '-fsanitize=address,undefined', '-fno-omit-frame-pointer',
                        str(SOURCE), '-o', str(binary)], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
        result = subprocess.run([str(binary), '--verify'], text=True, capture_output=True,
                                env={**os.environ, 'ASAN_OPTIONS': 'halt_on_error=1',
                                     'UBSAN_OPTIONS': 'halt_on_error=1'})
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stdout + result.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(result.stderr, '')
